title: Hotstart signal logbook: pool hysteresis & warmup breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
Personal scratchpad capturing commands run, log snippets, quick hypotheses and next actions while investigating repeated capacity thrash and slow warm paths for a Dedicated GPU pool (on-call night). Preserve transient diagnostics from pager session and follow-ups to convert into a formal incident postmortem later.

Context:
- Pool: dp-dedicated-eu-west-2/gpu-pool-4 (H100 nodes, 8x GPU)
- Symptom: rapid create-drain cycles of nodes (5-15m lifecycle), long warm tails (~3m) leading to request queueing and retries from controller
- Alerts first fired: 2026-03-09 23:20 UTC; pager escalation 2026-03-10 00:04 UTC

High-level observations:
- Autoscaler scales up aggressively on queue spikes, but new nodes often enter NotReady or have driver/container crashloops during bootstrap.
- Two failure modes: (1) node bootstrap fails (driver DS crashloop) due to package fetch errors; (2) node becomes Ready quickly but kv-cache priming is slow or OOMs so serving-runtime deems it not warm.
- Feedback loop: slow warm -> higher latency -> autoscaler perceives shortage -> scale-up -> bootstrap failures or slow priming -> scale-down when nodes are NotReady.

Commands & checks performed (chronological):
- kubectl config use-context rwinf-prod-eu-west-2
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-pool-4 -o wide 2026-03-10T00:22Z (6 nodes, 3 NotReady)
- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-23-45 | egrep -i "kernel|driver|taint|unsched" -> nvidia-driver-installer crashloop (OOMKilled init)
- kubectl logs ds/nvidia-driver-installer -n gpu-drivers --tail=200 -> downloader failed with 503 from packages-redwood.s3
- curl -v https://packages-redwood.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/cuda-runner/2.1.0/sha256 -> intermittent 503 matches infra metrics
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 on node ip-10-0-23-45 -> eviction of kv-cache-populator pods (OOMKilled)
- kubectl logs deploy/kv-cache-populator -n serving-runtime --since=20m -> prefetch stalled: "0/512 completed; latency 183s; missing shard 3"
- prometheus queries for container CPU and network egress to check warmup load patterns
- nvidia-smi & dmesg -> GPUs present but device plugin errors and driver mismatch messages

Error snippets captured:
- downloader.go: "failed to fetch object: status 503"
- kubelet: "Failed to setup device plugin: plugin API mismatch: server version 1.4, client 1.6"
- kv-cache-populator: "panic: allocation failed: unable to reserve 48GB for shard loader"
- serving-runtime: "model_load: shard 3 missing, falling back to remote fetch (cold)"

Working hypotheses (ranked):
1) Package distribution instability: S3 5xxs during bootstrap cause driver DS crashloops and node NotReady. Evidence: S3 503 spikes in timeframe + driver DS logs.
2) Autoscaler hysteresis too tight for spiky traffic: cooldown < real warmup causing oscillation. Need warmup-aware windows.
3) KV-cache/populator memory consumption sometimes exceeds available memory on new nodes resulting in OOM and prolonged priming.
4) Device plugin / kubelet minor version skew leads to API registration failures and restarts.
5) Large remote shard fetch patterns + limited egress bandwidth cause extended warm paths on initial load.

Quick validations performed:
- Grafana: confirmed elevated S3 503 errors between 2026-03-09 23:15 and 2026-03-10 00:40 UTC.
- kubelet --version on failing nodes: 1.31.2 vs control-plane 1.31.3 -> minor skew.
- Configmap diff: autoscaler stable-window was 30s for this pool.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Temporarily increased autoscaler stable-window from 30s to 180s for gpu-pool-4 to reduce churn (infra ops manual override).
- Rolled driver DS back to v2.0.9 (known good) to avoid hitting the new package path during window.
- Launched 2 pre-warm reserved nodes with nodeSelector preemptible=false to act as cache warmers for critical shards.

What I tried that regressed or didn't help:
- Turning off graceful drains caused more failed requests (reverted).
- Increasing kubelet eviction thresholds in template helped future nodes but not already-failing ones.

Post-mitigation snapshot (10-90m):
- Oscillation frequency dropped; pool reached steady capacity in ~6-8m (improved from 10-20m).
- 95p latency reduced ~30% but still above SLO; kv-cache completion still trailing on some nodes.

Raw trace snippets saved:
- [2026-03-10T00:17:18Z] ds/nvidia-driver-installer ip-10-0-23-45: failed to fetch: status 503
- [2026-03-10T00:19:34Z] kubelet: device plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = plugin API mismatch
- [2026-03-10T00:20:04Z] kv-cache-populator: prefetch shard=3 status=fetching url=s3://models-prod/shard-3 seg=0 tries=3
- [2026-03-10T00:22:12Z] autoscaler: scale_up pool=gpu-pool-4 delta=4 reason="pending-queue>threshold"
- [2026-03-10T00:25:07Z] autoscaler: scale_down pool=gpu-pool-4 delta=3 reason="node-not-ready:3"

Immediate follow-ups (owners):
- Evan Park (infra): pin & mirror package distribution, add robust retry/backoff + multi-region mirrors for driver artifacts.
- Diego Ruiz (serving-runtime): add readiness gating based on kv-cache-populator completion for critical model shards so nodes are not used until warm.
- Asha Kapoor (autoscaler): introduce warmup grace period tied to cache-populator metrics, not just k8s Ready.
- Hannah Lee (platform): evaluate product offering for reserved pre-warmed nodes and pricing trade-offs.
- Maya Singh (infra): add CI gate to prevent device-plugin/control-plane API mismatch, reconcile manifests.

Short checklist to close incident doc (me):
- Upload full driver DS logs artifact to incident folder (saved /tmp/maya/h100-driver-20260310.tar.gz).
- Create PR to add mirror + 5xx retry logic to driver-installer with circuit-breaker.
- Run 24h canary with driver v2.0.9 and monitor S3 client errors & bootstrap success rate.
- Draft design doc to gate node readiness on kv-cache-populator metrics.

Notes-to-self:
- Convert this scratchpad into timeline + graphs (CPU, network egress, s3 errors, scale events).
- Remind PM to freeze driver image upgrades until mirrors + retry logic are in place.

Linked artifacts (repeated for visibility):
- INC-4452 (JIRA)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/388
- Confluence: /display/INF/Pool+Warmup+Runbook

Status: draft - will expand with prometheus panels and timeline plots for the incident postmortem.
